findings: Three benchmark names are distinct in the pinned benchmark file. Previously reproduced duplicate-name overwrite is a checker robustness limitation, not an observed name collision in current fixture.

Fixture contains 10000 groups and 20098 media records, but DuplicateGroups initially mounts only first thirty groups: 100 big-group items plus 29 pairs = 158 cards. It does not render every one of the 10000 groups.
Fixture construction, all-selected set and kept-map creation occur outside measured benchmark callbacks. Full application state construction/default keep computation is not included.
Initial-load callback measures mount plus unmount. Toggle callbacks measure initial mount, rerender and unmount, not isolated toggle latency. No actual pointer/keyboard interaction occurs.
Each render/rerender supplies new no-op callbacks, which change memoized row props. This differs from stable callbacks in app and complicates interpreting row memoization gains.
Thumbnail loader is mocked and viewer returns null. jsdom benchmark has no real image decoding/network, browser layout/paint/GPU, scroll traversal or embedding detection.
No performance results generated in this review; fixture scope must accompany any future numbers.
limits: Static benchmark source review; no benchmark execution or optimization speed claim.
47/84 full files read; no production code changes.
